analysis.title: THINK Ahead: Your questions, answered
key_insights: ING's base case is more dovish and benign than market pricing: oil falls further, easing inflation, and central banks stop hiking after a final hike in December.

Weaker household balance sheets limit pass-through from higher energy prices to core inflation. Companies absorb the cost through lower profit margins. Major central banks could consider rate cuts towards the end of 2027.

Markets price virtually flat rate expectations beyond 12 months. The current curve resembles the 2007 hiking cycle more than 2008 or early 2023, when markets priced a larger decline after the near-term peak.

ING sees two conditions for a more humped curve (lower terminal rate): a material growth slowdown, or lower inflation risks. Growth remains robust, so ING sees the second as more likely and expects a repricing lower by mid-2027.
Europe's social safety net cushions lower-income households from the energy shock. The consumer-confidence gap between top and bottom income quartiles has not widened in 2026.
The eurozone savings rate has fallen since energy prices rose, cushioning consumption. Rising unemployment expectations make further declines in the savings rate unlikely.

US interest costs are 4% of GDP with a primary deficit of 2.5% of GDP. After the mid-term elections ING treats the primary deficit as locked in, since President Trump would likely veto Democrat tax and spending policies.

At an average borrowing cost of 3.6%, nominal GDP must grow 6.1% a year to hold debt-to-GDP at 100%. Nominal growth is closer to 5%, so the ratio looks set to climb. An AI-driven productivity boom could change this.

The ECB will be hesitant to restart bond purchases while governments do not adopt austerity. If French fiscal stress spreads while other eurozone members follow the fiscal rules, ING expects the ECB to use the Transmission Protection Instrument to ring-fence France.

The quits rate is the best leading indicator for US wage growth. It fell from 3% in 2022 to 2%, and wage growth slowed from 5.5% to 3%. ING calls this a low-hire, low-fire economy and expects benign national wage growth until quits rise.

ING expects the Fed to stay cautious on cuts for much of 2027, so policy is not an early tailwind for gold. Expectations of easing, lower yields and a softer dollar should support gold later, along with central bank buying and geopolitical demand.

US week ahead: Thanksgiving shortens the week after hefty falls in stocks and bonds driven by AI-outlook anxiety and Fed hike risk. ING expects core PCE on Wednesday to be hot, at 0.3% MoM against the 0.17% MoM pace consistent with 2% YoY.

tension_points.bull_case: ING's base case: oil falls, core inflation pass-through stays limited, central banks stop hiking after December and could consider cuts towards end-2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Market pricing implies virtually flat rates beyond 12 months, similar to the 2007 hiking cycle. Hot core PCE and Fed hike risk could keep the hiking bias.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A material growth slowdown or no decline in inflation risks would change the curve shape. ING expects a repricing lower by mid-2027 if inflation risks fall.
